summary: This bill modifies Medicaid disproportionate share hospital (DSH) payment adjustments by altering how hospital-specific DSH limits are calculated, allowing states to include certain individuals covered by other plans in their DSH calculations, and enabling states to use unspent DSH allotments from prior years under the new rules.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly impacts healthcare by modifying Medicaid disproportionate share hospital (DSH) payment adjustments. By allowing states to use unspent DSH allotments and modifying limitations, it aims to provide more financial support to hospitals that serve a high volume of low-income patients, which generally aligns with expanding public healthcare support.

The bill strengthens the social safety net by ensuring that hospitals serving a disproportionate share of Medicaid and uninsured patients receive adequate funding. This directly supports the healthcare component of the social safety net, preventing these hospitals from facing financial distress and ensuring care for vulnerable populations.

The bill's core purpose is to relax Medicaid DSH payment caps and allow states to make larger uncompensated-care adjustments to safety-net hospitals, directly increasing federal Medicaid expenditures.
By expanding Medicaid DSH payments to hospitals serving low-income patients, the bill constitutes government action to sustain safety-net care rather than relying on market competition.
